title: Jensen Huang’s Downfall Will Accelerate U.S.-China ‘Great Decoupling’
text:
Jensen Huang’s Downfall Will Accelerate U.S.-China ‘Great Decoupling’

Channel News Asia

Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

The following is an excerpt from an op-ed published in Channel News Asia on November 16,  2026, written by Diana Choyleva, Non-Resident Senior Fellow on Chinese Economy at ASPI's Center for China Analysis.The scandal engulfing Nvidia's Jensen Huang, who resigned as CEO on Thursday (Nov 12) after 33 years at the company he co-founded, could have consequences far beyond the fate of one of the world's most influential technology executives.With the woman linked to him suspected to be a Chinese spy, his extramarital affair has taken on geopolitical proportions, given Nvidia is at the centre of the US-China AI rivalry.Alice Huang is a former executive at Singapore-based cloud computing provider Megaspeed, a major Nvidia customer that has come under US scrutiny over concerns about the possible diversion of advanced AI chips to China. When the scandal broke, US intelligence officials reportedly believed that she was working for China's Ministry of State Security.No evidence supporting that allegation has been made public. On Thursday, US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a press conference that the Justice Department is investigating and there was not yet any conclusion about whether she was a Chinese spy.Whether she was a spy, whether Jensen Huang was compromised, or whether US national security was jeopardised remains to be established. Yet the political damage may already have been done.Read the full op-ed here.
